    StartersOatcakes and cheddarCrisp oatcakes served with sharp cheddar and apple chutneyHow to make it200g rolled oats50g butter, melted1 pinch sea salt flakes200g sharp cheddar4 tbsp apple chutneyMix the oats with the melted butter, salt and a splash of hot water.Roll thin and cut into rounds.Bake at 180°C for 20 minutes and cool.Serve with sliced cheddar and apple chutney.Thistle-topped smoked salmonWholemeal bread with lemon butter, smoked salmon, dill and capers, cut in squaresHow to make it50g soft butter1 lemon, zested6 slices of wholemeal bread200g smoked salmon1 tbsp chopped dill1 tbsp capersMash the butter with the lemon zest.Spread on the bread and top with smoked salmon, dill and capers.Cut into neat squares.Highland haggis bon bons, whisky creamA Scottish supperHow to make itAs written, serves 4Spiced lamb and oat haggis rolled into balls, crumbed and fried crunchy, with a whisky, wholegrain mustard and cream dipping sauce.Fry 400g lamb mince with a diced onion, then add 80g toasted oats, 1 tsp allspice, 1 tsp pepper, half a tsp nutmeg and 150ml beef stock and cook until thick.Cool and roll into 20 balls.Roll in flour, beaten egg and breadcrumbs and fry at 175°C for 3 minutes until crisp.Simmer 150ml cream with 2 tbsp whisky and 1 tbsp wholegrain mustard for 3 minutes for the dip.Black pudding with roast appleFuel for the blue face paint and Stirling.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsScotch broth and lambLamb neck simmered with barley, split peas, leeks, carrots and swedeHow to make it1kg lamb neck2.5 L water100g pearl barley100g split peas2 leeks, sliced2 carrots, diced1 swede, diced2 tbsp chopped parsley1 crusty loafsalt and pepper, to tastePut the lamb, water, barley and split peas in a large pot and bring to a simmer.Simmer gently for 1 hour, skimming now and then.Add the leeks, carrots and swede and simmer for another hour.Pull the meat from the bone and return it to the pot. Season and finish with parsley.Serve with crusty bread.Stirling venison with neeps and tattiesThe army's feast after StirlingHow to make itAs written, serves 4Venison backstrap seared rare and sliced, with buttery mashed swede, creamy mashed potato and a peppery whisky cream sauce.Boil 600g diced swede and 600g potatoes in separate pots until soft.Mash the swede with 30g butter and pepper, and the potatoes with 40g butter and 80ml milk.Season 800g venison backstrap with cracked pepper and sear in a hot pan 3 minutes a side for rare, then rest 8 minutes.Add 40ml whisky to the pan, then 150ml cream and 1 tsp cracked pepper and simmer 2 minutes.Slice and spoon over.SweetsScottish shortbreadButtery shortbread with rice flour, cut while warmHow to make it250g butter, softened130g caster sugar, plus extra to sprinkle300g plain flour60g rice flourBeat the butter with most of the sugar until pale, then work in the flour and rice flour.Press into a tin and prick all over.Bake at 150°C for 40 minutes.Cut while warm and sprinkle with caster sugar.DrinksWallace's heather honey whisky toddyHot Scotch whisky, honey and lemon with clove studded lemon wheelsHow to make it4 lemon wheels12 whole cloves160ml Scotch whisky4 tbsp heather honey1 lemon, juiced600ml just-boiled water4 cinnamon sticksStud the lemon wheels with the cloves.Into four heatproof glasses put whisky, honey and lemon juice.Top with just-boiled water and stir until the honey dissolves. Add a studded lemon wheel and a cinnamon stick to each.Scottish heather alePass it round before Stirling Bridge.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
